recent_posts.title: Nine Months of DevEx Improvement at Mercari Group
recent_posts.summary: Mercari Group implemented a company-wide DevEx improvement initiative over nine months, evolving from team-level efforts with mixed results to a dual-layer approach combining bottom-up team improvements with top-down organizational policies. The breakthrough came in Phase 2 when VPoE-led initiatives focused on Deep Work achieved 16% improvement in a single quarter by establishing clear policies like no-meeting time blocks and meeting consolidation. Success required three key roles (Executive Sponsor, Champion, Manager), proper structure with 6-12 month timebases, and connecting developer pain to business outcomes. Ongoing challenges include horizontal deployment across diverse organizations, measuring long-term business impact, and maintaining momentum across multiple quarters.

recent_posts.title: Capturing Network Packets in Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: Mercari's Network team shares two methods for capturing network packets in Kubernetes environments. The primary approach uses Ephemeral Containers with tcpdump to capture unencrypted traffic at the pod level, enabling developers to self-service debug without node access. This method works well with Istio service mesh by capturing on all interfaces to see plaintext traffic. A secondary node-level approach using GKE SSH and CoreOS Toolbox is available for platform teams investigating node-wide issues, though it only captures encrypted traffic. The procedures include specific kubectl commands, permission requirements, and file retrieval steps designed for production troubleshooting.

recent_posts.title: Designing “Mandates” for Safe and Flexible Recurring Payments
recent_posts.summary: Merpay developed a "Mandate" system to handle recurring payments across multiple payment methods. Unlike traditional implementations that tie mandates to single payment sources, Merpay's design allows customers to authorize future charges using combinations of points, balance, deferred payment, and credit cards. The system validates mandates through the payment creation API, ensuring safety for off-session payments. Integration with their Checkout Solution abstracts mandate complexity from developers, requiring only two simple steps: using Checkout for initial setup and calling CreateCharge in off-session mode for recurring billing. This approach is already live for Mercari Mobile's monthly subscription payments.

recent_posts.title: Building a Learning Culture with DevDojo
recent_posts.summary: DevDojo is Mercari's engineer-led training program that transforms onboarding into a collaborative learning ecosystem. Engineers design and teach courses based on real-world challenges, creating a culture of shared knowledge ownership. The program uses continuous feedback loops and retrospectives to evolve its curriculum, while kick-off sessions help instructors share best practices. Beyond technical training, DevDojo builds community by having instructors share real stories about incidents, migrations, and architectural decisions, helping new graduates understand how Mercari engineers approach problems collectively.

recent_posts.title: The Cost of Speed: A Battle against Cost, Debt, and Diverging Systems
recent_posts.summary: Mercari's Shops Enabling Team reduced system costs by 67% over one year by consolidating two divergent architectures. The three-person team unified search/recommendation systems, migrated 80+ microservices from Cloud Run to GKE while preserving developer experience, and standardized identity management using Mercari PAT. The migration involved strategic organizational design, AI-assisted refactoring, comprehensive observability, and iterative execution that maintained feature velocity while eliminating technical debt.

recent_posts.title: Supercharging User Engagement: How Mercari is Using Server-Driven UI to Reduce Time-to-Market
recent_posts.summary: Mercari's Growth Platform team implemented Server-Driven UI (SDUI) architecture through a feature called EGP Card to accelerate campaign deployment and reduce time-to-market. The solution allows UI configuration to be controlled remotely via JSON schemas rendered natively on iOS, Android, Web, and Flutter, eliminating the need for app releases when updating campaign designs. Key implementation challenges included versioning and backwards compatibility, cross-platform rendering consistency, personalization through placeholder replacement, and state management for interactive components. The team addressed these through graceful degradation, comprehensive testing automation, AI-assisted code generation, and custom component patterns. While requiring significant upfront investment, the SDUI approach dramatically reduced campaign iteration time from weeks to minutes and enabled rapid A/B testing.

recent_posts.title: Extending the Balance Service: Challenges in Implementing Multi-Currency
recent_posts.summary: Mercari's Balance team extended their double-entry bookkeeping system from JPY-only to multi-currency support. Key challenges included deciding where to store exchange rates (API at header level, database at source level for future flexibility), implementing flexible validation that accepts different rounding methods within reasonable margins, and designing reversal operations to use output-only exchange rates to prevent ledger imbalances. The team also recognized the importance of tracking both region and currency as separate dimensions, since currency codes alone don't uniquely identify legal jurisdictions.

recent_posts.title: Search Results Quality Monitoring with LLMs
recent_posts.summary: Mercari automated their search results quality monitoring by replacing manual review processes with LLM-based evaluation. Using Gemini 2.5 Pro, they implemented a system that scores search result relevance on a 0.0-1.0 scale based on Amazon's ESCI criteria (Exact, Substitute, Complement, Irrelevant). The solution provides both online monitoring of production queries (1,000 keywords weekly, 120 items each) and offline evaluation tools for pre-release testing. By combining product metadata with image data and standardizing evaluation prompts, they achieved consistent, objective quality assessments that replaced subjective manual reviews.

recent_posts.title: Engineering The Semantic Layer: Principles for Data at Scale
recent_posts.summary: A semantic layer acts as a translation bridge between raw data and business users, providing a single source of truth for metrics and definitions. By encoding business logic once and abstracting away SQL complexity, it eliminates inconsistent metrics across dashboards, reduces duplicated work, and enables teams to query data using business concepts rather than technical schemas. Mercari's implementation demonstrates how logical models, centralized metric definitions, and schema insulation create a scalable foundation that supports analytics, machine learning, and AI-driven tools while maintaining consistency across the organization.

recent_posts.title: Shipping English support for Mercari Japan across platforms
recent_posts.summary: Mercari Japan launched English UI support across iOS, Android, and web after years of preparation. The team leveraged existing i18n infrastructure built during a previous rebuild, used AI to review 15,000 strings and identify issues, then had human translators fix ~1,000 flagged items. Key challenges included cross-team alignment, QA testing for locale-specific bugs like truncated strings, platform-specific routing and locale handling, and backend microservices localization. Extensive dogfooding revealed issues like mistranslations and address input requirements. Phase 1 covers static UI; Phase 2 will tackle dynamic content and user comments with AI-driven translation.
